title: Joint River Commission formed
detail: Following the 19 March 1972 joint declaration to establish a permanent commission, the Joint River Commission was formed in November 1972.

title: Dry-season flow recognized as an issue
detail: In a joint declaration in May 1974, the two prime ministers acknowledged the need to augment dry-season Ganges flow at Farakka for Bangladesh and Kolkata port, and said an acceptable agreement should be reached before the barrage began operating.

title: Interim arrangement begins
detail: An interim agreement allowed experimental operation of the Farakka feeder canals for 41 days, from 21 April through 31 May 1975.

title: Five-year sharing agreement signed
detail: Bangladesh and India concluded a five-year Ganges water-sharing agreement after negotiations resumed.

title: Two-year memorandum signed
detail: The two governments signed a memorandum of understanding on water sharing for two years after the 1977 agreement expired.

title: Further memorandum signed
detail: Bangladesh and India signed another water-sharing understanding for three years.

title: Thirty-year treaty signed
detail: Prime Ministers Sheikh Hasina and H. D. Deve Gowda signed the Treaty on Sharing of the Ganga/Ganges Waters at Farakka in New Delhi. It entered into force on the date of signature for 30 years.
